inspection_summary: Inspected all 4,488 logical lines. The paper turns the explicit formula into a Lefschetz-style trace formula for the idele-class action on the noncommutative space of adele classes. Its semantic arc runs from the negative sign in prime-orbit comparisons to an absorption-spectrum/cokernel interpretation, proves local and S-local cutoff trace formulas, and isolates a still-conjectural global trace formula equivalent to RH for all relevant L-functions. The cutoff removes the artificial Sobolev parameter: critical zeros occur as spectral points, while off-line zeros contribute through harmonic measure as resonances. Appendices supply the homogeneous-distribution proof, identify the cutoff principal values with Weil's, and formalize the distributional transversality calculation. Formula extraction is frequently degraded, so exact constants and operators require the retained PDF, but the governing mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,795 lines. The source uses the preimages of the real and imaginary axes under zeta as an X-ray representation: their intersections mark zeros and poles, their branching marks derivative zeros, monotonicity orients curves, and region adjacency records value quadrants. This geometry supports argument-principle counts, two Speiser criteria for RH, and a sheet-based pairing between zeros and Gram points. Higher panels deliberately expose failures of Gram's and Rosser's laws, Lehmer pairs, derivative-controlled near-reconnections, and increasingly complex coils measured by S(t). The mathematical prose is usable, but many pages are primarily raster figures reduced to labels; those ranges were inspected and marked extraction-defective rather than inferred from unseen curves.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 878 logical lines. Assuming RH, the paper converts moment upper bounds into a tail problem for log|zeta(1/2+it)|, upper-bounds that logarithm by a short smoothed prime sum plus a controllable conductor term, and applies high moments of Dirichlet polynomials to obtain nearly Gaussian moderate tails and exponential large tails. The crucial conceptual move is that nearby critical-line zeros contribute with the favorable sign for an upper bound. The same template extends under GRH to unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal L-function families, where prime-square terms shift the Gaussian mean and hence the moment exponent. Formula extraction is visibly degraded but all prose mechanisms and theorem roles are recoverable.
